saturnus 0.9.0 lets your AI app use the calculators on the web page:
Claude, ChatGPT or Claude Code can read the display and the stack, press
keys, run RPL and look up commands in your browser tab, and you can watch
every call it makes.

## Get it

- **On the web**, nothing to install: <https://ractive.ch/saturnus/app/>
  (Chrome or Edge for a serial cable; every browser for the emulated
  calculator). AI access is on the web page only.
- **The desktop app** `saturnus_0.9.0_…` (on Linux `saturnus-app`), with a
  `-SHA256SUMS` file beside them:
  - macOS, Apple silicon: `.dmg`, signed and notarised, or `brew trust
    --cask ractive/tap/saturnus-app` once, then `brew install --cask
    ractive/tap/saturnus-app`;
  - Windows: `.msi` or `-setup.exe` for x86_64 (`x64`) and ARM (`arm64`);
  - Linux: `.deb`, `.rpm` or `.AppImage` for x86_64 (`amd64`, `x86_64`)
    and ARM (`arm64`, `aarch64`). Add yourself to the `dialout` group to
    use a serial port.
- **The command-line tools** `saturnus` and `satx`: `cargo install`,
  Homebrew `ractive/tap`, Scoop `ractive`, or the archives and Linux
  packages below.
- **Libraries** on crates.io, all at 0.9.0, unchanged apart from the
  version.

## AI access

- Open a calculator, choose **Connect your AI app…** in the sidebar or the
  command palette, and add the address shown to your AI app as a custom
  connector (claude.ai, Claude Desktop, ChatGPT's developer mode) or MCP
  server (Claude Code). When it asks for a code, type the 6-digit code
  saturnus shows.
- The AI app can list the calculators, read the display, the stack and
  variables, press keys, run RPL and functions, and look up commands with
  the reference. Storing or purging a variable asks you first: Allow,
  Always allow (for that app until you reload or disconnect it) or Don't
  allow.
- The connection goes through the relay https://tab-mcp.ractive.ch, built
  on [tab-mcp](https://github.com/ractive/tab-mcp). What it passes and
  keeps: <https://ractive.ch/tab-mcp/>.
- The sidebar says whether an AI app is connected and offers Disconnect;
  a broken connection is tried again by itself.
- **The AI's calls**, closed by default: every call with its arguments and
  how it ended, and the connection's events, beside the calculator.
